comedians.name: Abby Govindan
comedians.profile_html:
In August 2026, during an Edinburgh Fringe run, The Guardian reviewed Pushing 30, Abby Govindan’s hour about love, big tech, marriage pressure, misinformation, and patriarchal expectations. “Patriarchy is not just a south Asian problem,” she says. The review called her delivery easygoing, conversational, and heartfelt.

Govindan grew up in Houston and made her comedy debut at Caroline’s on Broadway in December 2017, at 20. Her official biography puts Indian American family life, internet virality, and the pursuit of stand-up at the center of her early work.

She has folded screenshots, pranks, and PowerPoint-style visuals into story-driven stand-up. She once convinced social-media users and media outlets that she created Emily in Paris; her official site notes that she did not.

In 2025, Govindan appeared on Scam Goddess and Last Things First, and brought the solo Off-Broadway show How to Embarrass Your Immigrant Parents to SoHo Playhouse. In 2026, she appeared on SBS Spice.

comedians.name: Alonzo Bodden
comedians.profile_html:
In October 2026, a Zofunny Monthly post found Alonzo Bodden writing about friends’ illnesses and deaths, postponed knee surgery, and the decision to stop deferring pleasure. “I am continually, sadly reminded that life is promised to no one,” he wrote. His stand-up draws on current events, race, media, and everyday observation.

Bodden grew up in St. Albans, Queens, then spent about a decade as an airplane mechanic before training mechanics at McDonnell Douglas. Teaching made him comfortable before a room; a comedy-writing course graduation show gave him his first time onstage. He began doing stand-up in Los Angeles in 1993, at 30, and later broke through at Montreal’s Just for Laughs. “I never looked back,” he said. “I knew that this was what I was going to do.”

His delivery is conversational. The Showtime specials Who’s Paying Attention? (2011), Historically Incorrect (2016), and Heavy Lightweight (2019) were followed in 2026 by How Do You Spell Moth?, released through Dry Bar Comedy and Angel. On television, he won NBC’s third season of Last Comic Standing after finishing runner-up in season two, and played Alonzo in five 2014 episodes of Californication.

comedians.name: Anjelah Johnson-Reyes
comedians.profile_html:
In May 2026, “Ugly Baby” arrived on YouTube, Anjelah Johnson-Reyes’s seventh hour-long special and her directorial debut. Filmed over two sold-out shows at Los Angeles’s El Rey Theatre, it covers motherhood in her 40s, fertility, pregnancy, postpartum life, relationships, and family generations. The material moves through personal stories, impressions, and characters.

Raised in San Jose, California, Johnson-Reyes was an Oakland Raiderette before moving to Los Angeles in 2005. A free church joke-writing class got her into comedy; “Nail Salon” was among her first jokes. She joined MADtv in 2007, playing Mỹ Linh, Tammy, and fast-food employee Bon Qui Qui, whose “I’M A CUT YOU” became the line. Her comedy returns to extended family, marriage, motherhood, aging, and daily irritations. Netflix tagged her 2015 special “Not Fancy” as Witty and Clean-Cut.

The Family Reunion tour sold more than 200,000 tickets across more than 100 U.S. theater shows in 2025 and 2026.

Her screen work includes Curb Your Enthusiasm, Ugly Betty, Superstore, and Hulu’s Life & Beth. In May 2024, she hosted Tubi’s eight-episode My Crazy Quince.

comedians.name: Daniel Sloss
comedians.profile_html:
In July 2026, The List found Daniel Sloss discussing two sitcoms in development after time away from touring following the birth of his daughter in 2024. “One is about an angry Scottish comedian. The other is about being an angry Scottish person in America.”

Sloss began writing and performing in 2007 after his mother met Frankie Boyle at a conference. Boyle gave him early access to the comedy circuit. He made his Edinburgh Fringe stand-up debut in 2008, aged 17. His shows have since traveled through 55 countries and nine New York off-Broadway seasons.

The 2018 Netflix specials DARK and Jigsaw cover the death of his sister, Josie, and relationships. In 2019’s Daniel Sloss: X, he addresses gender expectations, toxic masculinity, and the sexual assault of a close friend. The structure often starts provocative or slapstick, then turns toward personal reflection.

Later releases include SOCIO in 2022, HUBRiS in 2024, and CAN’T, released on DanielSloss.com in December 2025. He has also appeared ten times on Conan, according to his official biography.

comedians.name: Dave Chappelle
comedians.profile_html:
In August 2026, the Associated Press reported that Dave Chappelle was scheduled to host Lauryn Hill’s Diaspora Calling! festival.

Born in Washington, D.C., Dave Chappelle split time between the Washington area and Yellow Springs, Ohio, after his parents separated. He attended Duke Ellington School of the Arts and moved to New York in 1991 for the stand-up club circuit, as outlined in his career background. He starred in the 1996 sitcom Buddies, then co-created and starred in Comedy Central’s Chappelle’s Show, which premiered in 2003.

Dave Chappelle builds long anecdotes from personal experience and cultural observation, covering race and racism in the United States, American politics, fatherhood and celebrity culture. Netflix released The Dreamer in 2023. His other specials include 2017’s The Age of Spin and Equanimity, 2019’s Sticks & Stones, and 2021’s The Closer.

comedians.name: Desi Banks
comedians.profile_html:
In April 2026, Forbes caught up with Desi Banks as he leaned into his “Your Favorite Cousin” identity and prepared for the forthcoming film Boyz Trip. “I look at myself as a comedian, not just a social media comedian,” he said.

Raised on Atlanta’s east side, Banks began posting sketches on Vine in 2012 and started doing stand-up in 2017. His background includes Cedar Grove High School, college football at Morehead State and Georgia State, and a sociology degree earned in December 2015.

Banks played Fonk the Freak in a 2022 episode of Sherman’s Showcase, appeared on Season 6 of The Shop: Uninterrupted in 2023, and joined Ms. Pat on a 2025 episode of We Got Time Today.

He has described the stage as a proving ground. Once the audience is with him, he can be freer with the material.

comedians.name: Dovi Neuburger
comedians.profile_html:
Dovi Neuburger draws on yeshiva culture, family expectations, faith, and dating, adjusting the context for audiences less familiar with Jewish practice. A September 2026 Unpacked profile noted his effort to bring Orthodox Jewish comedy beyond its usual audience. One early joke he counted as a major success used “Love on the Spectrum” as a misdirection after a premise about Jewish dating.

Neuburger left NYU Law after one semester and first tried stand-up at a Hanukkah show at Young Israel of the Upper West Side. He nearly quit after bombing. Then came a successful Purim set at Stand Up NY in March 2023, followed by a Gotham Comedy Club class, open mics, and more shows. His material includes his father’s criticism of a mezuzah’s placement in his apartment and the difficulty of getting a blanket into a duvet cover.

His official site says he regularly opens Elon Gold’s theater dates and founded and produces the StandUp for Israel Comedy Tour. On BrainStorm with Sony Perlman in 2024, Neuburger discussed leaving law school. In 2026, he appeared on AND HERE’S MODI to discuss a seven-show Israel run, the matchmaker process, a Birthright trip, and being a rabbi’s son.

For live rooms, Neuburger adjusts the cultural explanation without sanding down the specifics. Ami Kozak told Unpacked that he brings “proper standup insight to the Jewish world” and makes specificity feel universal.

comedians.name: Iván Fematt La Mole
comedians.profile_html:
“Qué necesidad de ir a un reality show a que te humillen, te critiquen y te insulten”. In an October 7, 2026, post reported the next day by POSTA México, Iván Fematt La Mole criticized the premise of entering a reality show to be humiliated, criticized or insulted. He named no program or contestant.

Iván Fematt La Mole emerged from Monterrey television and radio. On Acábatelo, he played Markitos, Empanadín, Maricela, Oso Dammy and El Guardia. He competed on Prime Video’s 2019 second season of LOL: Last One Laughing and hosts the Multimedios late-night program Buenas noches Don Fematt.

His stand-up pulls from television, newspapers, weddings and daily experience. “Voy sacando del día a día, leyendo el periódico, viendo la tele, voy a una boda y de cada vivencia saco una experiencia o un dato que voy incorporando,” he has said. The material is improvised, audience-near and rooted in Monterrey and northern Mexico. “No soy mucho de meterme con la gente,” he has also said.

At a November 2024 performance in Tijuana, Semanario ZETA reported that Iván Fematt La Mole worked with an audience of more than 1,000 people, using stories contextualized to the border audience.

comedians.name: Karen Morgan
comedians.profile_html:
In 2026, Angel began streaming Put Some Butter On It, Karen Morgan’s third Dry Bar Comedy special. Angel describes it this way: “Karen Morgan believes brides who give dress codes for guests should have their weddings ruined.” Her material covers parenting, marriage, aging and generational differences.

Karen Morgan began her professional comedy career in 2005, after taking a local comedy workshop while raising three children. A tape sent to Nickelodeon’s Search for the Funniest Mom in America made her one of seven finalists from more than 1,000 applicants. She earned a BFA from the University of Georgia in 1986 and practiced as a trial attorney, a background documented in her University of Georgia profile.

Her 2023 YouTube special Glamour Shots In The Dark includes chapters called “Cassette Tape,” “Perilous Playground,” and “Mean Candy.” Earlier Dry Bar specials include Go Dawgs! from 2020 and Rub Some Dirt On It from 2023. In May 2024, she performed on The Talk’s “Stand Up at THE TALK” segment.

comedians.name: Keegan Tindall
comedians.profile_html:
In September 2026, CBS aired Keegan Tindall on “Comics Unleashed with Byron Allen”, alongside Luenell, CJ Marrinan, and Michael Turner. His work includes stand-up and original online sketches with a playful, absurd streak.

Tindall is from South Jersey and based in New York. On Robert Kelly’s September 2024 “You Know What Dude?” appearance, “Eating Dog Food,” he discussed being burned after a drunk driver hit him, his family, and his father’s habit of eating dog food. A 2023 appearance on “Mindful Metal Jacket” carried the subtitle “Burn Victim Guy.”

The New York Comedy Festival named him a Comic to Watch in 2024. Moontower Comedy notes that he was passed at the Comedy Cellar. In November 2025, he wrote and voiced the comedy animation “Gnome Bacon.”

comedians.name: Marito Lopez
comedians.profile_html:
In September 2026, The Secret Sex Lives of Muslim Women introduced Marito Lopez as “the first straight cis man to ever enter The Secret Sex Lives of Muslim Women.” He discussed sobriety, his conversion to Islam, faith, sex, and dating.

Lopez began performing comedy in 2009. Born in El Salvador, he immigrated to Canada with his family as a child and grew up in Calgary, Alberta. After working there, he relocated to Toronto and performed in New York City. A talent-management profile lists The Stand and New York Comedy Club among the rooms where he is a regular.

Lopez voiced Marito in 17 episodes of Gary and His Demons from 2018 to 2023, played Carlito in four 2024 episodes of One More Time, and competed on Roast Battle Canada against Jarrett Campbell and Sophie Buddle. He was featured in the March 2022 The New Wave of Standup episode devoted to him. His 2026 Apple TV special followed the February 2025 release of his comedy album LatinXXX.

comedians.name: Marlon Wayans
comedians.profile_html:
In August 2026, Real Laughs heard Marlon Wayans describe a new hour taking shape in clubs, with another special expected within months. “I stay on stage and I keep grinding and it just makes me better,” he said. His stand-up runs on physical humor, impressions, and personal stories.

Wayans has worked since his 1988 film debut in I’m Gonna Git You Sucka. He became widely known through The Wayans Bros. and the Scary Movie films. His 2018 Netflix special Marlon Wayans: Woke-ish and HBO Max’s Marlon Wayans: God Loves Me make room for family, race, relationships, fear, and his own mistakes.

That turn lands hardest in 2024’s Good Grief: “I’ve been dodging depression for the last three years. I lost my momma three years ago. And let me tell you y’all something, ain’t no pain, ain’t no nothing like losing your momma.” In a CBS News interview about grief, stand-up, and acting, he put his career drive plainly: “I don’t know if I’m chasing, or if I’m running from something!”

comedians.name: Mo Amer
comedians.profile_html:
In October 2026, Mo Amer sold out Radio City Music Hall. Dave Chappelle introduced him as a surprise guest; Jon Stewart, Ramy Youssef and Shane Gillis also appeared. The Houston Chronicle reported that Amer was the first Arab stand-up comedian to headline the roughly 6,000-seat room. “To switch gears and do my own show there and then have Dave go on there as a surprise guest, introduce me, it was so special man,” he later said.

Born in Kuwait to Palestinian parents, Amer arrived in Houston after his family fled the Gulf War and grew up in Alief. He started doing stand-up as a teenager in 1999. His Houston background runs through stories of family, citizenship, refugee experience and Texas.

His Netflix specials include Mo Amer: The Vagabond, 2021’s Mo Amer: Mohammed in Texas, and 2025’s Mo Amer: Wild World. He works in English, Arabic and Spanish, with Muslim and Arab American life at the center. “My mother is a gansta,” he says.

That material fed Mo, the Netflix comedy-drama he co-created, executive produced and stars in. Its second season arrived in January 2025. Amer also appeared on Hulu’s Ramy and joined WTF with Marc Maron, Episode 1619 in 2025.

comedians.name: Nikki Glaser
comedians.profile_html:
In September 2026, after transgender influencer Briel Adams-Wheatley publicly objected to an onstage joke, Nikki Glaser apologized privately and said she would remove it immediately. “I HATE anti trans jokes of all kinds, and to think I may have added to that rhetoric is disgusting to me,” she said.

Glaser began doing stand-up in college in 2002 after growing up in the St. Louis area. Her specials, from 2016’s Nikki Glaser: Perfect to the 2024 HBO/Max hour Nikki Glaser: Someday You’ll Die, cover sex, dating, sobriety, beauty, aging and death. In a 2023 Salon interview, she said, “I’m always trying to keep it very real.”

Glaser created, hosted and executive produced Comedy Central’s Not Safe with Nikki Glaser, then hosted and executive produced Max’s dating series FBoy Island. She hosted Saturday Night Live in November 2025 and the Golden Globe Awards in 2025 and 2026. Her Hulu special Nikki Glaser: Good Girl premiered in April 2026. The Stunning Tour launched that year.

comedians.name: Tony Hinchcliffe
comedians.profile_html:
On The Joe Rogan Experience #2522 in July 2026, Tony Hinchcliffe discussed the backlash to his George Floyd joke from The Roast of Kevin Hart. “I’m going to go for it,” he said.

Hinchcliffe grew up in Youngstown, Ohio, and graduated from Ursuline High School in 2003. A December 2007 Vindicator profile found him in Los Angeles, working restaurant jobs and getting onstage at open mics. He later worked at The Comedy Store and wrote for Comedy Central’s The Burn with Jeff Ross and roast episodes involving James Franco, Justin Bieber, and Rob Lowe.

His solo specials include Netflix’s 2016 release One Shot and 2021’s Making Friends, uploaded to YouTube. Netflix released Kill Tony: Kill or Be Killed in April 2025, followed by the solo special Man of the People in June 2026.

He is closely associated with Kill Tony, the touring podcast where aspiring comics perform one-minute sets before improvised interviews and critiques from Hinchcliffe and a guest panel. He has called it “the most spontaneous and improvised show that is out there.”
